questions.q: Three vessels of equal volume contain gases at the same temperature and pressure. The first vessel contains neon (monoatomic), the second contains chlorine (diatomic) and third contains uranium hexafluoride (polyatomic). Arrange these on the basis of their root mean square speed  \left({v}_{rms}\right)$ and choose the correct answer from the options given below:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The RMS speed is given& ${v}_{rms}$~$= \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$.

The temperature and pressure is same for all the gases. So the speed is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass of the gases.

${v}_{rms} ( mono ) = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{4 \times {10}^{- 3}}}{v}_{rms} ( dia ) = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{71 \times {10}^{- 3}}}{v}_{rms} ( poly ) = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{352 \times {10}^{- 3}}}$

${v}_{rms } ∝ \dfrac{1}{M}$

Hence,

${v}_{rms} ( poly ) < {v}_{rms} ( dia ) < {v}_{rms} ( mono )$.

questions.q: Energy of 10 non rigid diatomic molecules at temperature $T$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { Degree of freedom }(f)=5+2(3 \mathrm{~N}-5) \\
& \qquad f=5+2(3 \times 2-1)=7 \\
& \text { energy of one molecule }=\frac{f}{2} K_B T
\end{aligned}$
energy of 10 molecules
$=10\left(\frac{\mathrm{f}}{2} \mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{T}\right)=10\left(\frac{7}{2} \mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{T}\right)=35 \mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{B}} \mathrm{T}$

questions.q:
Following statements are given
(1) The average kinetic energy of a gas molecule decreases when the temperature is reduced.
(2) The average kinetic energy of a gas molecule increases with increase in pressure at constant temperature.
(3) The average kinetic energy of a gas molecule decreases with increases in volume.
(4) Pressure of a gas increases with increase in temperature at constant volume.
(5) The volume of gas decreases with increase in temperature.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Average kinetic energy of a gas molecule is given by& ${KE}_{avg} = \dfrac{3}{2}KT$.

Pressure of a gas in terms of rms speed is given by~$P = \dfrac{1}{3}ρ{v}_{rms}^{2}$.

As~$K{E}_{avg} ∝ T$, so \left(1\right)$~is correct, \left(2\right)$ is incorrect, statement \left(3\right)$ can not be said.

Note : Statement (4) is correct only if we consider it at constant volume and not constant pressure. Ideally, this question must be bonus but most appropriate answer is option (A)

$

(B) the mean collision time between the molecules decreases.

(C) the mean free path remains unchanged.

(D) the mean collision time relations unchanged.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know mean free path

$\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{N}{V}\right)\pid^{2}}$

N = no. of molecule

V = volume of container

d = diameter of molecule

Velocity constant and no. of molecules are same. So mean free path remains same. As temperature increases no. of collision increases so relaxation time decrease.

questions.q:
The total kinetic energy of $1$ mole of oxygen at $27 ° C$ is :
[Use universal gas constant $( R ) = 8 . 31J{mol}^{- 1}K^{- 1}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the kinetic energy can be written as

$K = \dfrac{f}{2}nRT . . . \left(1\right)$

Since oxygen is a diatomic gas, the number of degrees of freedom is $5$.

Thus, from equation (1), it follows that

\begin{cases}$K & = & $\dfrac{5}{2} \times$1 \times8 . 31 \times300J \\ & = & 6232 . 5J\end{cases}

$

questions.q: Two moles of helium gas is mixed with three moles of hydrogen molecules (taken to be rigid). What is the molar specific heat of mixture at constant volume?  \left(R = 8.3J / molK\right)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
\left({C}_{v}\right)mix = \dfrac{{n}_{1}{C}_{v1} + {n}_{2}{C}_{v2}}{{n}_{1} + {n}_{2}} = \dfrac{2\left(\dfrac{3}{2}R\right) + 3\left(\dfrac{5}{2}R\right)}{2 + 3}$
$= \dfrac{3R + \dfrac{15}{2}R}{5} = \dfrac{21}{10}R = 17.4J / molK

questions.q: A vessel contains $14g$ of nitrogen gas at a temperature of $27 ° C$. The amount of heat to be transferred to the gas to double the r.m.s. speed of its molecules will be : (Take $R = 8 . 32J{mol}^{- 1}k^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The RMS& speed of a gas at a given temperature is given by,& ${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$.

Therefore, to double the RMS speed, the temperature should be increased to four times the initial temperature. Therefore,

${T}_{f} = 1200K, {T}_{i} = 300K, \text{and}n = \dfrac{14}{28} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

The volume of the vessel will remain~the same therefore, the process is an isochoric process. Therefore,

$Q = n{C}_{v}\Delta T = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{5R}{2} \times 900$

$⇒ Q = 9360J$

questions.q: A flask contains Hydrogen and Argon in the ratio $2: 1$~by mass. The temperature of the mixture is $30 ° C$. The ratio of average kinetic energy per molecule of the two gases  \left(\dfrac{Kargon}{Khydrogen}\right)$ is: (Given : Atomic Weight of $Ar = 39 . 9$)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the average kinetic energy per molecule of a gas at any temperature& $T$~is given by

${K}_{avg} = \dfrac{3}{2}{k}_{B}T$

where,~${k}_{B}$~is Boltzmann constant.

From above equation, it can be concluded that the average kinetic energy per molecule is independent of the molecular weight of the gas.

Hence, the required ratio is~$1: 1$.

The root mean square speed of smoke particles of mass $5 \times {10}^{- 17}kg$ in their Brownian motion in air at NTP is approximately.

[Given $k = 1 . 38 \times {10}^{- 23}JK^{- 1}$]

According to Kinetic theory,&

Average& kinetic energy& of a gas molecule& $= \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{rms}^{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}kT$

Thus,~${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3kT}{m}}$

At NTP,~$T = 293K$

Putting the values, we have

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{3 \times 1 . 38 \times {10}^{- 23} \times 293}{5 \times {10}^{- 17}}}$

$\approx 15mms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A gas mixture consists of $2$ moles of oxygen and $4$ moles of neon at temperature $T$. Neglecting all vibrational modes, the total internal energy of the system will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The internal energy of a gas is given by& $U = n{C}_{V}T$.

A diatomic gas has~$3$~translational and~$2$~rotational degrees of freedom. A monoatomic gas has~$3$~translational degrees of freedom.

Hence, the internal energy of the mixture~$= {n}_{1}{C}_{V1}T + {n}_{2}{C}_{V2}T$

$= 2 \times \left(\dfrac{5R}{2}\right)T + 4 \times \dfrac{3R}{2}T = 5RT + 6RT$

$= 11RT$

questions.q: Two moles of an ideal gas, with $\dfrac{{C}_{P}}{{C}_{V}} = \dfrac{5}{3}$, are mixed with three~moles of another ideal gas $\dfrac{{C}_{P}}{{C}_{V}} = \dfrac{4}{3}$. The value of $\dfrac{{C}_{P}}{{C}_{V}}$ for the mixture is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let $n_1,n_2$ be the number of moles of gases $1$ and $2$.
We have $\dfrac{C_{p_1}}{C_{v_1}}=\dfrac{5}{3}$ and We know $C_{p_1}=C_{v_1}+R$
$\therefore \dfrac{5C_{v_1}}{3}=C_{v_1}+R,\dfrac{2C_{v_1}}{3}R_1,C_{v_1}=\dfrac{3R}{2}$
$A$ and $C_{p_1}=C_{ v_ 1 }+R=\dfrac{5R}{2}$
Also, $\dfrac{C_{ p_ 2}}{C_{ v_ 2 }}=\dfrac{4}{3}$ and
$C_{p_2}=C_{v_2}+R$
$\therefore \dfrac{4C_{ v_ 2 }}{3}=C_{ v_ 2 }+R, \dfrac{C_{ v_ 2 }}{3}=R,C_{ v_ 2 }=3R$
$C_{ p_ 2}=C_{ v_ 2 }+ R=4R$
Now $C_{ v_ {mix} }=\dfrac{n_1C_{ v_ 1 }+n_2C_{ v_ 2 }}{n_1+n_2}=\dfrac{2\times \dfrac{3R}{2}+3\times 3R}{2+3}$
$=\dfrac{3R+9R}{5}=\dfrac{12R}{5}$
$C_{ p_ {mix} }=\dfrac{n_1C_{ p_ 1 }+n_2C_{ p_ 2 }}{n_1+n_2}=\dfrac{2\times \dfrac{5R}{2}+3\times 4R}{2+3}$
$=\dfrac{17R}{5}$
$l_{mix}=\dfrac{C_{ p_ {mix} }}{C_{ v_ {mix} }}=\dfrac{17}{12}=1.4166=1.42$.

questions.q: The temperature of an ideal gas is increased from $200K$ to $800K$. If r.m.s. speed of gas at $200K$ is ${v}_{0}$. Then, r.m.s. speed of the gas at $800K$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

At& $200K$, the rms speed is given by

${v}_{0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3R \times 200}{M}} . . . ( 1 )$

At~$800K$, the rms speed is given by

$v ' = \sqrt{\dfrac{3R \times 800}{M}} . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and solve to calculate the required speed.

\begin{cases}\dfrac{v '}{v0}$& = & $\dfrac{\dfrac{3R \times 800}{M}}{\dfrac{3R \times 200}{M}}$\\ & = & $\sqrt{\dfrac{800}{200}}$\\ & = & 2 \\ & ⇒ & v ' = 2{v}_{0}\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: $2$ kg of a monoatomic gas is at a pressure of $4 \times {10}^{4}Nm^{- 2}$. The density of the gas is $8kgm^{- 3}$. What is the order of energy of the gas due to its thermal motion?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Internal energy is the energy due to thermal motion.

The internal energy of an ideal gas given by

$U = \dfrac{f}{2}nRT$ (for~$nmoles$)

$U = \dfrac{f}{2}\left(PV\right) = \dfrac{f}{2} \times P \times \dfrac{M}{ρ}$~(Since,~$f = 3$ for~a monoatomic gas.)

$U = \dfrac{3}{2} \times 4 \times {10}^{4} \times \dfrac{2}{8}$

$= 1.5 \times {10}^{4}J$
So, the order of energy due to thermal motion is~${10}^{4}$
